# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

Policy Playground: a FastAPI demo of [openshell-annotate](https://github.com/ilanh/openshell-annotate) on NVIDIA OpenShell. Each card on the page (`app/static/index.html`) runs one action inside the sandbox and shows whether the policy allowed or denied it, compared with the action's expected verdict.

**The `@openshell` comments in the source are the policy.** `openshell/policy.yaml` is generated by `make policy` and must never be edited by hand. After changing any `@openshell` directive, regenerate it, or `make drift` fails.

## Commands

```bash
make help              # list targets
make dev               # run locally with uv on :8080, unsandboxed (DENY rows come back ALLOW/ERROR)
make scan              # list every @openshell directive with file:line
make policy            # regenerate openshell/policy.yaml from annotations
make lint              # flag unannotated net/fs/exec (expected: example.com and api.github.com:80 calls, /opt/forbidden and /app writes, curl subprocess info)
make drift             # fail if policy.yaml is out of sync with annotations (CI check)
make sandbox           # build image (runs `policy` first) and start it in OpenShell, forwarded to :8080
make diff-logs         # fetch sandbox logs and map denials back to suggested directives
make down              # delete the sandbox
```

Variables: `ENGINE=podman` for Podman, plus `SANDBOX`, `IMAGE`, `PORT`. `make install-annotate` installs the pinned `openshell-annotate` CLI (`ANNOTATE_VERSION`) into `~/.local/bin`. There is no test suite. To verify, run the actions in the sandbox ("Run all" on the page, or `POST /api/run/{id}`).

## Architecture

- `app/actions/__init__.py` holds the `@action(id, group, title, expect, why, op)` decorator and the `REGISTRY`. `load()` imports `net`, `fs` and `proc` in that order, which is also the display order. `op` is the exact operation, built with `http_op(method, host, port, path)`, `curl_op(argv)` or `file_op(mode, path)`; `http_op` takes parts rather than a URL so `lint` doesn't report the metadata as a second URL literal. An action function returns `(outcome, detail)` or `(outcome, detail, extra)`, where `extra` may carry `http_status`, `exit_code` and the full `output`. `Action.run()` maps `PermissionError` to DENY and any other exception to ERROR (with the traceback as output), and sets `match = outcome == expect`.
- `app/rules.py` explains, read-only, which entry in `openshell/policy.yaml` governs each `op` (host+port, binaries incl. parents, access/L7 allow and deny rules, audit, fs roots, or "no rule → default deny"). It is for display only; OpenShell decides. `/api/actions` returns it per action as `rule`.
- `Action.source()` uses `inspect` to read the `@openshell` lines inside each function at runtime, so the page shows live `file:line` directives. Put a directive inside the function body, directly above the call it covers.
- Each module infers verdicts in its own way. In `net.py`, HTTP 403 or a proxy/connection error means DENY (OpenShell's proxy answers 403). In `fs.py`, Landlock returns EACCES. In `proc.py`, curl's exit code 7/35/56 or HTTP 403 means DENY.
- Some code is deliberately left unannotated (`example_com`, `github_port_80`, `write_forbidden`, `write_app`) so it produces DENY rows and `lint` findings. Don't "fix" it. `httpbin_post`, `postman_status` and `python_icanhazip` use `@openshell ignore kind=net` because their host is already declared and the rule itself (L7 allow, `deny=`, `bin=`) is what denies them.
- `app/main.py` declares `fs read /app`. Without it the server can't load its own code, page or policy. Endpoints: `/api/actions`, `/api/run/{id}` and `/api/policy`, which serves the generated YAML.

## Constraints

- OpenShell matches egress binaries on the real executable path, not symlinks. `/usr/local/bin/python3.12` must stay the same in three places: `openshell-annotate.toml` (`[languages].python`), `PY` in the Makefile, and the Dockerfile `CMD`/base image. Change all three together.
- Binary rules also match ancestor processes, so a subprocess (curl) inherits the Python server's egress rules.
- `include_workdir = false` keeps the sandbox strict. Only `/app` (read), `/data` (write) and OpenShell's baseline are reachable.
- Leave `WORKDIR` out of the Dockerfile. OpenShell rejects an image workdir that the non-root sandbox user can't use (`WorkspaceValidationFailed`). Uvicorn is started with `--app-dir /app` instead.
- The Dockerfile has `@openshell ignore kind=all scope=file` because build-time commands run before the sandbox exists.
- Network policies reload live (`openshell policy update`). Changes to filesystem, landlock or process sections need the sandbox recreated (`make sandbox`).
- OpenShell 0.1.6 doesn't log filesystem denials, so `diff-logs` only sees network rows.
- On Docker Desktop for macOS, the gateway may need `[openshell.drivers.docker] supervisor_network_mode = "bridge"` (see README).
